note: Every number of the cloud deck. Units are camera heights at the fit of frame 3150 (1 unit = 0.1725 degrees on the sphere). The chart has its origin under the storm, y along the view on the ground, x to the right. maps: the height maps from the finest to the widest, centre and size in units, pixels per side (the web set holds half).

tool.note: Numbers of the tools in assets-src/jupiter/deck that lay the canvas back onto the sphere. heightGain: gain of the depth tool's relief (deck/relief.py), fitted so the storm's walls stand as in the image. reliefSigmaPx: the relief is the depth tool's range over the smooth sphere's range, less its own mean over this many canvas pixels. reliefReach: the relief fades with the range, gone at this many units. depthBlurPx: blur of the image heights in canvas pixels (a map may name its own). resolveFactor, minResolve: the scale the image resolves on the ground is its footprint along the view times resolveFactor, at least minResolve units. trustFrom, trustTo: the image's heights are used where that scale is under trustFrom and not at all over trustTo. heightBlur: least blur of the heights in units (a map may name its own: the fore map holds the ground under the flight at the scale the canvas resolves there, so a crest of the heights stands where the canvas shows it). trustFeather: blur of that trust in units. slopeMax: no stored height may rise faster than this over the ground (a cone is laid over every top and the higher of the two kept), so the march, which sizes a step by the height over the ground and this slope, cannot step over a wall. heightRange: the lowest and highest height the maps store. reliefFade: the heights go to zero from reliefFade[0] to reliefFade[1] units from the point under the fit camera. plateRelief, plateReliefScale: where the image's heights are not used the near map takes the depth tool's relief of the top down near plate, with this gain, less its own mean over plateReliefScale units. roughBand, roughSpread, roughLevel: a plate's alpha is its own roughness, the energy between the scales roughBand in units, spread over roughSpread units, 1 at roughLevel.

canvas.note: The picture the fields are laid back from: the wide canvas of the earlier build (the approved close image in the middle, aprons at the same scale on all sides, recipe in RECIPE.md), with the approved image itself pasted over the middle. scale: canvas size over the size of the approved image. feather: image pixels from the border of the approved image over which the paste fades in. depthShrink: the depth tool runs on the canvas shrunk by this.

core.note: Inside the approved image the fields take their colour from the core: the approved image at scale times its size (the upscale tool, then the fine fold detail of the earlier build, recipe in RECIPE.md under the terrain deck, steps 2 and 11). lockPx: above this many core pixels the core is held to the tone of the approved image. feather: image pixels from the border of the approved image over which the core fades in.

light.note: azimuthDeg: the direction to the Sun on the ground of the chart, measured from the chart's x axis toward its y axis, as the approved image shows it. The function detail is embossed along it and the air is measured about it.

look.note: Numbers of the shader in clouds.ts. shell: lowest and highest height of the layer the march runs in. march: slack added to the slope of the ray when a step is sized by the height over the ground, least step in pixel footprints, a hit counts under this many footprints, most steps. foot: least cosine between ray and ground in the footprint, the footprint is cut into taps when it is longer than this times its width, most taps (the haze). blend: share of a height map's half width where it starts to give way to the next and where it ends. join: the same for the levels of the guide. anisotropy: taps of the texture filter. cloud: the detail made by code, see its own note.

cloud.note: The detail made by code: everything finer than the guide's cut. One field of rounded tops per wave length and per age of the wound coordinates (deck.json life.flow.wound): in every cell one top, alive between its forming and its dissolving. waveUnits: the largest wave; octaves: how many halvings of it there may be. leastFeet: the smallest wave drawn, in footprints of the pixel as it lies in the wound coordinates; fade: the wave, in the same measure over leastFeet, from which a wave has its full strength. taps: the most places along a drawn out footprint at which the field is read. fall: the power by which the strength of a wave falls with its length under the largest. tops: how much brighter a top is than the mean, in the logarithm of the light per unit of the field. slope: the same for a slope of one toward the Sun's azimuth; the slope is divided by the stretch of the wound coordinates, so a form drawn out to a thread is as low as it is narrow. tint: per channel, what is added to tops for the colour, so tops are paler and lanes deeper than the guide. ages: the weight of each age. lifeSeconds: the least time from forming to dissolving; a wave of lifeWaveUnits lives twice as long, a cell up to twice its wave's time. octaveTurn and octaveShift, ageTurn and ageShift: the turn in radians and the shift in cells between the fields of two neighbouring waves and of two ages, so none repeats another. cell: reach is the radius of a top in cells, jitter the share of the cell over which its centre is free. field: the mean and the variance of the field of one wave and the variance of its slope along one axis, measured by assets-src/jupiter/deck/puffs.py; the mean is taken off and the variance keeps the mean light of the ground the same with and without detail.

air.note: The air between the camera and the deck, written by deck/air.py: one layer of haze over the deck, as thick as the eye of the approved view stands high (deck-fields.json view.eye) and equally dense everywhere. The share of the plates' light that comes through is exp(-layer.per times the length of the ray's path through the layer). From an eye at or above the layer's top that length follows from the sine of the angle between the ray and the ground at the point alone, and the eye is never under it (the surface view flies at that height or above), so the table is kept by that sine. The light the air adds (by that sine and by the turn of the ray away from the Sun's azimuth, mirrored) is what the cell means of the approved view have over that share of the plates' cell means, never less than 0. layer.per: the layer's strength for one unit of path. layer.flat: from the first knot at or over this sine downwards both tables are held. At every height those sines lie in the last pixels under the limb (at frame 3037 every sine under 0.056 lies within 10 px of it), and a table that still changes there draws its own profile over the far ground. sinRange: the sines of the first and last knot, spaced by ratio. knots: count over the sine, count over the turn from 0 to 180 degrees. clear: between these sines the air ends, so a steep ray sees the plates as they are. minTexels: texels of the view chart a cell needs. smooth: blur of the added light in cells. The weight by which the air is gone is not kept here: it is read from the place on the ground (place.json scene.air), the same at every height of the camera, so the ground the approved view saw keeps the air it was painted in from the first frame of the dive and nothing comes in as the camera sinks. assets-src/jupiter/deck/lift.py and lift-measure.json are the history of the weight solved by film time (the largest level step was 4.84 a frame then). History of the share: up to the second named commit of round 2 it was the one measured on the approved view (green 0.14 from sine 0.063 down and 0 under 0.02), which is not a share of light but how little of the plates' far field the approved view shows; a ground point crossed its step in 8 frames of the dive. air.py still prints it.

flight.note: The flight of the surface view: one flight that takes the dive's motion at its first frame and hands the rise its motion at its last. seconds: its length. The camera passes the pose of the approved image at the middle. Up to the middle the forward speed over the ground goes from startUnitsPerSecond with the power of the elapsed share (endUnitsPerSecond is what that law would reach at the end), and the camera comes down: startAbove units higher at the start, falling with the sinkPower of the share of the way still to go, so it stays near the bottom plane of the approved view and little ground shows that the image never saw. bend: from the end of the judged middle frame's own shutter the push bends into a track across and on into a pull back up the lens's own line, which is the line the rise leaves along. The heading of the flight turns from straight ahead to straight back along the lens, through the right where through is -1 and through the left where it is 1 (to the right the eye stays over ground the approved image saw until the rise has lifted it; to the left the frame's bottom left corner left that ground four frames after the seam, while the eye was still low), on a smooth step that has no turn at either end, and the climb comes in with that step raised to climbPower, so the track across stays level and the camera lifts only as it pulls back. The speed over the camera's own height rises in a straight line from what the middle frame has to endPerSecond, so it never falls. The way is summed once in steps of 1 over stepsPerSecond and read between them through a cubic with the true speeds, so it holds at any fraction of a frame; beyondSeconds is how far past the seam the table reaches, straight on. ease: units and unitsPerSecond are the old cut of the way; they act only inside the shutter of the judged middle frame, so that frame's camera stays what it was to the byte. aimPx: at the middle the film's camera is the camera of the lay back to the pixel. The lay back counts each pixel of the picture at its upper left corner, so the ray of the picture's middle lies this many picture pixels right and up of the lens's line and the camera is turned onto it; the turn that the film's camera drift (director rig, drift) has at that instant is taken out as well. Both make one fixed turn of the whole flight: the motion stays what it was, and the judged frame shows the approved image where the image has it.

view.note: The image field: the canvas laid onto the heights in a chart that matches the view of the fit camera (deck/view.py), so no texel is stretched at the fit pose. Since the fit camera looks its own picture up (image), the chart is seen only where that camera saw nothing or saw the ground too steeply; what it holds there is made by the fill below. thetaDeg: the chart's span of azimuth about the point under the fit camera, from the chart's y axis toward x. psiNearDeg: its nearest ground as the angle of the ray under the horizon. horizonMargin: units of ground distance left out before the horizon. pixels: the size of the chart the geometry is worked out on. fine: the stored chart holds this many texels per such pixel each way. imageMargin: canvas pixels at the canvas border that are not used. Ground the fit camera did not see is found per stored texel by the same test the shader uses (image.hidden against the stored range), so chart and shader agree to the texel. steep: ground whose texel is over this many times longer than on level ground counts as unseen too. Both are filled along the view: the colour of the ground just beyond the gap's far border (the mean of fillMean pixels) runs into the gap and passes to the colour just before its near border, which leaves out hiddenSkip pixels, so a narrow gap is never darker or lighter than both its sides. fillEdge: the outline of the steep ground is smoothed by this many pixels before it is laid on the fine grid. fillSmooth: the distances to the two borders are averaged across the view over this many pixels. fillNear: the ground before the gap (the crest that hides it) is mirrored in only over the last part of the way from the far border to the near one, from this share on; before it the gap holds the far ground alone, which is what a camera ahead of the fit pose sees first. fillAcross: the two border colours are averaged across the view over fillAcross[0] pixels at the border and over fillAcross[1] pixels from fillAcross[2] pixels into the gap on, so a wide gap carries no stripes. fillDetail: the fine structure (what is left of the canvas after a blur of fillDetail[3] pixels) of the ground mirrored about the two borders is added fillDetail[0] times, from fillDetail[1] to fillDetail[2] pixels inside the gap on; nearer to a border the gap is the plain run of colour. fillLength: a filled texel is stored this many times the gap's width longer than level ground where it holds no fine structure, so the shader's own detail fills it at the scale of the pixel. lengthRange: the shortest and longest ground length of a texel the alpha channel stores, by ratio. fade: canvas pixels from the canvas border between which the image field fades out.

limb.note: Glow over the limb as a table over (sunward place of the limb point, tangent height). deck/limb.py measures it on the approved image: python3 limb.py clear, render frame 3150 at the draft tier, python3 limb.py RENDER.png. cover = tangent heights between which the glow stops hiding the sky patch. Rows are spaced by the square root of the height.

plates.note: Top down plates of the place, made from the approved close image by assets-src/jupiter/plates (recipe in assets-src/jupiter/RECIPE.md). Units and chart as the maps; size and pixels are x then y. They hold albedo in the globe's coding (values above white kept), so the globe shows them as the deepest levels of its patches. order: the order in which the plates are made. parents: the plate a canvas is enlarged from; without one the canvas starts from the globe's own albedo at the place, with the flow frozen as in place.json (globeBlurPx: how soft that is in plate pixels). inset: a finished finer plate laid into the canvas at its own place. grade: one colour, the median over the laid back image within gradeRadius units of the vortex of the close image over the globe's albedo, both at a scale of gradeScale units. The plates were made as the close image divided by it. Since round 2 of the second note no program reads it: the plates hold the close image's light, and the globe and the deck both draw them over place.json solved.light, the globe's own light on a ground that faces the Sun at the place, with no exposure by height or time. useBlur: the laid back image is used where its own blur along the view is under useBlur[0] units, and not at all over useBlur[1]; beyond, near the image's horizon, the globe's own structure stays. flatten: from flatten[0] to flatten[1] units of ground distance from the close camera the laid back image gives up its tone above a scale of flatten[2] units to the globe's, because there its tone is the haze of a low view, not the cloud. carry: outside the laid back image the canvas carries the image's tone on from the border (measured at a scale of carry[0] units) and lets it go over carry[1] units. free: outside the laid back image the repaint is tied to the canvas at a scale that grows by this many pixels of blur per pixel of distance from the border. softPx: plate pixels of blur per unit of the image's own blur along the view, which marks unresolved parts as unfinished for the repaint. parentBlurPx: the blur of a level enlarged from the level above. clear: the globe's own structure is taken away within clear[0] units of the vortex (fading out to clear[1]) by a blur of clear[2] units, so the repaint closes the storm of the close image all the way round and the globe's small oval, which is that storm seen from far, does not stand beside it. bandPx: width and blur, in plate pixels, of the unfinished band along the border of the laid back image. finishedPx: blur under which the canvas is kept as it is. lock: the repaint keeps its own structure below lock[0] times the canvas blur (at least lock[1], at most lock[2] pixels) and takes the canvas above. lockGain: strength of the repaint's own structure. hiddenError: fixed point error of the lay back, in units, over which a place counts as hidden from the close image. feather: width of the join in units. nest: the near plate keeps its own repaint inside nest[0] units from its centre and is the mid plate beyond nest[1], measured with the power norm nestPower (a rounded square); the mid plate is the near plate made smaller inside the same shape. upward: assets-src/jupiter/plates/upward.py takes the place as the plates show it from above (fore, near and mid plate nested as the globe nests them) and writes it, reduced by area to the texel of a level above the mid plate, into the levels named in levels: far is the far plate (in the plates' coding), wrap is the globe's wrap and patches are its three patches (there divided by the grade, times the tone and calm fields, as the globe shows the plates). All three are written: the globe carries the place from the hold down (one Jupiter outranks the bytes of the hold inside a small disc round the place), so no height brings the storm in. from: the commit whose wrap and patches carry no place; the tool starts from those on every run, so a second run writes the same bytes. border: full within the first distance in units from the vortex, none from the second. ring: kept says that the far plate the tool starts from carries the place already (the tool's own earlier output), so in the far plate only the disc where the border is full is written again and the ring between the two distances stays as the first run mixed it; a second run then writes the same bytes. spread: the point spread, in units of the chart, through which the place is written into each level of the globe's own imagery (a Gaussian of that width, in linear light, after the reduction by area). Each level is a picture of the planet with a point spread of its own, and nothing written into it may be crisper than the picture is: assets-src/jupiter/plates/spread.py measures it on the level as it stood before the place was written (the sharpest tenth of its clean edges, the fiftieth of its texels with the steepest gradient whose profile rises without a turn over 6 texels to either side): 1.30 texels of the wrap, 1.10, 1.20 and 1.02 texels of the three patches, in the full set; the web set takes the same widths in units and is only softer. For the wrap the octaves say the same: unfiltered, the place held 7.92 and 6.53 levels (rms of luma) in its two finest octaves where the great red storm of the same picture holds 4.26 and 4.05; through 1.25 texels it holds 2.43 and 3.99 (review of round 2, condition b of 23:34: in the hold nothing in the place is crisper than the hero's own detail round it). marginDeg: how far past the border the tool looks for texels.

beyond.note: The canvas' own ground laid on past its borders (MAIL 1074 item 2) by plates/beyond.py, no image model; recipe in assets-src/jupiter/RECIPE.md, step 17. from: the commit whose plates and heights the script reads, so a second run writes the same bytes. box: the part of the chart it works on (x from, x to, y from, y to), on a grid of the fore plate's texel. floor: added to a colour before its logarithm. insetPx, openPx: the canvas' ground is what the fit camera saw at least insetPx canvas pixels inside its frame, opened by openPx grid texels, its largest piece. zone: the ground to fill lies outside the canvas' ground, whole to borderUnits[0] from it and gone at borderUnits[1], whole to reachUnits[0] from the fit eye's ground point and gone at reachUnits[1]; filled: the share of laid ground round a texel from which it counts. source: where pieces may come from: the canvas' ground more than borderUnits inside its border and insetPx inside its frame, nearUnits from the eye's ground point, further than stormUnits from the storm's centre, without the glints (blue over glint[0] times red, the brightest above glint[1] in 100) and without the towers (the height over its mean within towerUnits, above towerShare in 100), these opened by openPx and widened by marginPx grid texels. So no piece is of the eye or of a tower. flow: the frame the pieces are laid in, log polar about the storm's centre (turns columns round, rings rows outward from innerUnits, the seam at axisDeg), where a shift is a turn about the storm and a scale, so a piece keeps its grain along the flow at its new place. pieces: the search in that frame for the source whose detail fits what lies beside it (seed of the first guess; flatUnits and heightWeight: the detail compared is colour and height less their mean within flatUnits; levels, passes, steps, reaches: the search from coarse to fine; toneWeight, scaleWeight, useWeight: the cost of another tone, another scale and a source used before; gapUnits: the least distance of a source from its target; together, arcFloor: the pull to lie beside the neighbour's source and the carry of the tone along the flow). splitUnits: the laid ground keeps the tone carried along the flow above this size and takes the pieces' detail below it. edge: inside the canvas' frame the plates take the canvas itself (its lay back blurred by layBlurPx), whole to insidePx[0] canvas pixels from the frame and gone at insidePx[1]. under: one body (condition i): where the fore plate hides the near plate the near plate is the fore plate filtered, whole to under[0] of the fore plate's half size and gone at under[1], inside look.join, so no texel with weight in the film changes by it. The mid plate is not written: the haze's light reads it under the near plate (clouds.ts sunAt, haze lightBlurUnits), and written as the near plate filtered it moved the final 3150 by up to 4 levels. preview: the pictures written to out/work/jupiter/beyond.

move.note: The place stands on a storm the globe shows from orbit: the eye of the pale spiral oval east of the great red storm, where the globe's Sun stands as low as the close image shows it (place.json oval). assets-src/jupiter/plates/move.py lays the plates that reach beyond the painted storm on that ground: the globe's own imagery there with the flow at rest (softened as globeSoftenPx says) times the globe's light at the place (place.json solved.light). plates: the plates it writes. keep: per plate, the radius in units round the vortex inside which the painted plate stays as it was baked (read from the commit named in from) and the radius from which the plate is the globe's ground alone; between the two they blend smoothly. So the painted storm is the eye of the globe's own oval and the oval's spiral arms run round it. shade: see its own note. After it run plates/tone.py, plates/calm.py and plates/upward.py, which writes the storm into the far plate and into the globe's own imagery (upward: levels and border), so that the globe carries the place from the hold down and no height brings it in.

shade.note: The storm keeps its own shade past the painted disc: the tone of the kept paint against the hero ground in a ring just inside the border, by direction about the vortex, is carried onto the hero ground beyond the border and let go between the two radii of reach, in units from the vortex. Only shade, never a lift. So the dark side of the storm ends as a soft shadow on the oval and not as a cut edge, at every height alike.

image.note: The fit camera looks its own picture up: a point of the deck that the fit camera saw takes its colour from the canvas at the pixel where that camera saw it (deck/image.py writes the canvas, the core at twice its scale for the approved image, and the range the fit camera saw along every ray), so the frame at the fit pose is the approved image, and from any other pose every point keeps the colour it had. A point the fit camera did not see (farther along its ray than the stored range) takes the fill of the view chart. rangeShrink: canvas pixels per stored range, for the full and the web set. rangeLog2: the least and the greatest stored range as powers of two. hidden: a point counts as seen while it lies less than hidden[0] of the stored range beyond it, and as unseen from hidden[1]. sharpen: the footprint of a lookup in the canvas is taken this many times its true size. quality: of the stored pictures. march: slack, least step and hit distance in stored pixels, most steps, of the tool march. reach: units from the point under the fit camera beyond which the deck is the smooth sphere. steep: a point the fit camera saw so steeply that one pixel of the canvas is drawn over more than steep[0] 1080ths of the frame height (pixels of the 16 by 9 master, whatever the format) passes to the fill of the view chart, fully from steep[1] on; below that the canvas is shown as it is and the shader's own detail fills the scale it lacks.

tone.note: The tone of the approved view as a smooth field over the ground, written by assets-src/jupiter/plates/tone.py to deck-tone.bin (three stacked blocks of pixels x pixels, 16 bit, value times scale): the approved view laid on the ground over the plates, both blurred by blurUnits, carried out smoothly past the ground the view saw, and led back to 1 between the fade distances from the point under its camera. The plates are multiplied by it at every height of the camera and by both programs, so the ground the view saw and the ground beside it have one tone from above. Up to round 46 the tone came in with the height of the camera (lift), and with it a second limb and a bank of pale cloud faded in place on the way down and up; that weight is gone. known: the view counts fully within the first distance in units from the point under its camera and not past the second. The same two distances end the approved view itself where the deck draws it, so its footprint on the ground has a soft round edge that is the same from every height. imageBlurPx: blur of the view before it is laid down. marginPx: rim of the canvas left out. range: least and most ratio.

calm.note: A second smooth field over the ground, written by assets-src/jupiter/plates/calm.py to deck-calm.bin (three stacked blocks of pixels x pixels, 16 bit, value times scale; pixels must equal tone.pixels, because the loader lays it beside the tone field in one texture). The ground is multiplied by it wherever it is multiplied by the tone field: the plates at every height of the camera, by both programs, and not the approved view itself. It changes two things the plates paint east of the storm, which from above read as faults. hue: where the ground outside the near plate's own repaint is colder than its surround, it is led to the hue of the warm ground around it. The measure is (blue - red) / (blue + red) of the ground blurred by blurUnits; the first number of cold is none and the second is full, the same way round for warm; darkBias weights a second blur towards the dark, so bright cloud tops inside a cold area do not hide it. The warm ground is carried in over surroundUnits; the target is at least lift times its brightness. The gain of a channel is at most the number most, all three channels scaled together so the hue holds, and at least the number least. softUnits blurs the mask and the gain. nestShare is the share of the near plate's own repaint above which hue does nothing. shade: the storm's cast shade in the near plate ends at the straight line where that plate gives way to the globe's own picture (plates.nest). The shade is carried on past that line: the ground outside is darkened to the level carried out from inside (carryUnits; inside is where the repaint's share is over the number inside, the ground outside is measured where it is under the number outside), fully up to the first distance of reach from the storm's centre and not at all from the second, that distance moved by a seeded value noise (noise: wavelength and amplitude in units; seed), and only where the inside is darker than the outside by the ratios in dark (none at the first, full at the second) and between the rows (chart y: off, on, on, off). lift: inside, the shade is lifted by up to the third number, rising from the first to the second distance from the storm's centre, so the step into the carried shade is small. edgeUnits: the field is led back to 1 over this distance inside its own border. preview: zoom and exposure of the before and after picture the script writes to out/work/jupiter/calm.

above.note: How the ground looks from above the air, so the far field of the surface view's scene is the globe's far field at the handover. Knots lie evenly in the square root of the sine of the angle between the ray and the ground (0 at the horizon, 1 straight down). gain: the light of the ground is multiplied by it. air: light added on top, in the scene's own units before the exposure. Both act by the weight by which the air is gone (place.json scene.air, read from the place on the ground). Every gain is 1 and all added light is 0 today, so the tables change no pixel. Measured at frame 3024 on stills of both sides: the globe alone (beauty/side=orbit/noplace) over the scene, medians per bin of the sine; under a sine of 0.2 the spread of the globe no longer follows the scene, so there the rest is added light.
above.evenNote: even: the share of the mix between the look under the air and the look from above that is taken in the logarithm of the light (1: the same ratio of light for the same step of the weight, so the far ground does not turn pale in the lowest tenth of the weight; 0: the straight mix). At a weight of 0 and of 1 the picture is the same either way. floor: the least light that enters the logarithm.

life.note: What moves in the surface view while the camera flies (mail 230, mail 1307). The ground is matter in a steady flow (flow): heights, the guide's colour and the detail made by code are read where their matter stood at the middle of the surface view (frame 3150), so every form is carried along its streamline, sheared where neighbouring streamlines run at different speeds, and nothing turns as a rigid body. No picture is scrolled or bent: the guide holds nothing finer than its cut (deck.json guide), so it is the matter's colour, and every finer form is made by code. storm: centre is the middle of the oval in chart units (also read by the tools of the plates). haze: two rigid sheets of cloud, thick.units thick, their middle at heightUnits over the datum (both above the relief, which stays within about 0.1), one on each side of the storm (side -1 south, 1 north of the line through the storm centre along the jet; a sheet begins between its two edgeUnits from that line and ends between its two reachUnits from the centre), drifting along the jet at unitsPerSecond (east is positive; the two go opposite ways, as the jets on the two sides of an anticyclone do). The density of a sheet is a function of its own point, the same at every height inside it: banks (bankUnits, warp) made of fibres along the jet (fibreUnits, fibreOctaves, fibreShare, fibreWarp), value noise in octaves (lacunarity, octaveGain, octaveShift, warpSeed), cover the two thresholds. What a ray shows of a sheet is its density along its way through it (mail 1021): the pattern is read at thick.taps points along the run of the ray between the upper and the lower face of the sheet and averaged, and each octave is faded (octaveFade) where the larger of that run and of the pixel's footprint (a 1080th of the frame height, a pixel of the 16 by 9 master, whatever the format) is long against the octave. The cover is taken of the faded noise with its two thresholds moved apart by what the faded octaves lost: thick.spread is the standard deviation of one octave of the noise, sqrt((26 / 35)^2 / 12), and a smoothstep of half width a is the distribution of a bell of variance a x a / 5, so the full width grows to sqrt(width^2 + 20 x spread^2 x the share of variance lost). A sheet whose pattern is averaged away keeps its mean density, not the cover of its mean. Steep and near a sheet is a bank with its parallax; grazing and far it is a veil with no pattern to slide over the ground. Neither the eye's height nor the clock enters, only the ray and the footprint. A sheet lightens what lies behind it by depth over the cosine of the view (at least minCosine) with the low passed colour of its ground (lightBlurUnits) times glow, so it takes the tone of its ground; that light is weighted by forward [g, gain] as min(gain x ((1 - g) / sqrt(1 + g x g - 2 g c))^3, 1), c being the cosine between the view ray and the direction to the Sun, so thin cloud shows where one looks toward the Sun and nearly vanishes where one looks down on it (measured: without the weight the south sheet lay as a pale mist band over the foreground at 3060 to 3135); on the deck it lays a shadow of shadowDepth where the Sun's ray passes through it (the one Sun of the place, solved.sun of place.json, which also lights the day side; the run of that ray through the sheet is averaged in the same way; the shadow is not faded by the pixel's footprint, it lies on the ground whoever looks at it), tinted by shadowTint, displaced by the height between sheet and ground, fading over softUnits where the ground reaches the sheet. Both count only where the ground is sunlit (lit: thresholds on the warmth of the low passed ground). flash: lightning inside the dark blue cloud. At each site (at in chart units as stored, radiusUnits) an envelope e = sum of strength x u x exp(1 - u) runs, u being the time since an event over riseSeconds. Two things follow from it. The cold pixels (cold: thresholds on blue against red, the sum of the two never taken below core.floor so that the black of the plate does not switch the mask; bright: thresholds on luminance, darker pixels take the share surround) are multiplied by exp(gain x e x exp(-q)), q being the squared distance over radiusUnits squared. And light is added: glow x e x (exp(-q x core.tight) + core.spill x exp(-q)) x the square root of the luminance of the pixel, a small bright heart with a wide faint spill that keeps the forms of the cloud it lights. The events [seconds from the middle, strength] were drawn once from seed and are listed, so the light is a function of time alone; a glow needs riseSeconds (about 4 frames) to its peak and fades over about 20, so nothing strobes; no event is alight at the middle (frame 3150) or at a handover. proof.cameraHeld: true holds the camera of the surface view at the pose of frame 3150 while time runs, for the life only sheet; false in the film.

flow.note: The matter of the place moves in one steady flow, the curl of one stream function, so nothing gathers and nothing thins; no part of it is a rigid body. unitsPerSecond: the fastest speed of the storm's own turn, V. Storm: about life.storm.centre the speed at the distance r is V times 2 s^2 / (1 + s^4), s = r over scaleUnits, counter clockwise seen from above; the turn in degrees a second is fastest at 0.76 of scaleUnits and nothing at the centre, so every ring shears against its neighbours; between the two fadeUnits the storm's own speed goes to nothing. jets: zonal winds, east on the storm's south flank and west on its north flank, share of V at their fastest, one whole wave of east and west every acrossUnits across the belts; their stream function is led to nothing inside the two partUnits from the storm's centre, so the jets part and pass round the oval. eddies: small vortices of the same form at their own centres, share of V (negative is clockwise), each led to nothing between its fadeUnits. Every carried field (heights, guide, detail) is read where its matter stood at the middle of the surface view (frame 3150): the place is carried back along the flow by the midpoint rule over the whole time, which runs on without a bound and without a reset. wound: the detail made by code is read in wound coordinates, the place where its matter stood before the fastest ring of the storm had turned by turnDeg (one age each), so the shear of the flow itself has drawn every form out along its streamline. assets-src/jupiter/deck/wound.py follows the flow back from every point of a polar grid about the storm's centre out to reachUnits (pixels: round, then out, the rows even in the square root of the distance) in steps of stepSeconds and writes deck-wound.bin with its ranges in wound.json; beyond the storm's reach the flow is the straight jets and the same place is found in closed form, and between the two closedUnits, where both hold, the program passes from the one to the other.

guide.note: The colour of the matter, written by assets-src/jupiter/deck/guide.py: the ground the plates paint (the plates joined as before, times the tone and the calm field, in the scene's light), cut by a Gaussian of cutUnits on the ground, in the chart of the body. Nothing finer than the cut is in it and no eye is in it: every program reads it by the ground point alone. levels: centre and size in units, pixels of the stored picture for the full and the web set, work: the grid the cut is made on. Beyond the mid level the far plate is the guide as it is (its own texel is wider than the cut).
